description_full: Paycom Software, Inc. provides cloud-based human capital management (HCM) solution delivered as software-as-a-service for small to mid-sized companies in the United States. The company offers functionality and data analytics that businesses need to manage the employment life cycle from recruitment to retirement. The company's HCM solution offers payroll applications comprising better employee transaction interface, payroll and payroll tax management, payroll card, Everyday, Paycom pay, Client Action Center, expense management, garnishment administration, and GL concierge applications; talent acquisition, including applicant tracking, background checks, on-boarding, e-verify, and tax credit services; and talent management applications that include employee self-service, compensation budgeting, performance management, position management, Paycom learning, certification management. The company also offers time and labor management, such as time and attendance, scheduling, time-off requests, and labor allocation solutions. Its HCM solution provides manager on-the-go that gives supervisors and managers the ability to perform a variety of tasks, such as approving time-off requests and expense reimbursements; direct data exchange; ask here, a tool for direct line of communication to ask work-related questions; document and checklist; government and compliance; benefits administration; COBRA administration; personnel action and performance discussion forms; Paycom surveys; retirement reporting; report center; and affordable care act applications, as well as Clue, which securely collects, tracks, and manages the vaccination and testing data of the workforce; and MyCom is a communications tool that provides organizations with a central place to share information with employees. Paycom Software, Inc. was founded in 1998 and is based in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

financial_summary: Paycom Software, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $10.9B market cap on $2.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years and +25% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 36% against a 11% cost of capital — a 25-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 83% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $408M in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.50× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 14% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 28% operating margin runs 21pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.19x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+7.1% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 535 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 66% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 12% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 47% and a beta of 1.15, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $153.2M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 51% in the 2020 crash and 36% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $233 (margin of safety -4%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 70%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $130 to $418 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 46% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.7% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 16 covering analysts target $271 on average, 12% above the price.
The price implies 15.6% annual cash-flow growth.
prof: ROIC of 36% clears the cost of capital of 11.0% by 25pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.39).
It runs a 83% gross margin and converts 20% of revenue into free cash flow, or 14% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.50x.
ROE of 26% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (4.4x equity multiplier).
It spends 13.8% of revenue on R&D and 5.8% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The company holds more cash than debt.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 14.3% over 3 years, 19.5% over 5 years and 24.8% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 12%).
At current returns, reinvesting 40% of profits supports about 14.4% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 25.1% a year over five years.
Capex runs 1.5x depreciation (13.2% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
own: Insiders own 14.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 93%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (8 sales, net $2.7M sold).
It returns 3.8% a year to shareholders (3.0% in buybacks and 0.6% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 5.3% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 5,770 employees, each generates about $356K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and revenue has grown 26.8% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $71K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $4.5M (13x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (9/10, lower is better).
